findings_addressed.oracle: Control case: file without #pragma once included twice across two process() calls on the same preprocessor instance yields repeated_field count == 2 (independent oracle proving _included_files resets between calls). Gate case: file with #pragma once included twice across two process() calls yields once_field count == 1, proving _pragma_once_files (not _included_files) is the active guard because _included_files is reset by process() on line 116 but _pragma_once_files persists across calls.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/hexpat/preprocessor.py line 395, remove the block `if _PRAGMA_ONCE_RE.search(content): self._pragma_once_files.add(resolved_str)` so that #pragma once files are never added to _pragma_once_files; the second process() call would then find the file absent from both sets and inline it again, making combined.count('once_field') == 2 and the assertion fail.

notes: The original test used a single process() call with two #include directives in the same source string. Within one process() call, _included_files accumulates across the whole call, so the second include was blocked by _included_files rather than _pragma_once_files - the #pragma once mechanism was not isolated. The hardened test calls process() twice on the same preprocessor instance (which resets _included_files on line 116 but preserves _pragma_once_files), plus adds a control case with a file lacking #pragma once that correctly appears twice, confirming the experimental setup.
